title: Tech Note: Clusters: Using Saved Sets Effectively - Part II

historical_commentary.text: This second half of a two-part series covers how to actually retrieve data using pre-built "clusters" of saved sets (following Part I's coverage of creating and maintaining those clusters), a manual performance-optimization technique for speeding up database queries in the classic 4D language. Saved sets remain part of current 4D, but the query optimizer, indexing improvements, and (for ORDA-based access) the lazy-loading entity selection engine introduced in later 4D versions have significantly reduced the need for this kind of manual clustering technique for most modern applications.
related_updates: 4D's classic query engine and indexing have been substantially optimized in versions since 2005, reducing the performance gap this manual clustering technique aimed to close
ORDA's entity selections (introduced 2017/v16 R2+) provide lazy-loaded, cursor-like access to large record sets, addressing similar performance concerns with a different, more modern mechanism
